title: Which gas leaks fastest?
hook: Two gases at the same temperature leak through a pinhole. Which empties first?

knows: that molecules move faster when hot
doesNotKnow: that at one temperature lighter molecules move faster, with speed scaling as one over the square root of mass

misconception: At the same temperature all gas molecules move at the same speed.
objective: The learner can say that at equal temperature helium escapes through a pinhole about 2.6 times as fast as nitrogen, because lighter molecules move faster (speed scales as 1/sqrt(molar mass)).

claims.text: The molar mass of helium is about 4.003 g/mol and of nitrogen gas (N2) about 28.014 g/mol.
claims.source: IUPAC standard atomic weights: He 4.0026, N 14.007 (N2 = 28.014).

claims.text: Through a pinhole, the rate of escape of a gas is proportional to one over the square root of its molar mass (Graham's law), so helium escapes about 2.6 times as fast as nitrogen at the same temperature.
claims.source: Graham's law (Atkins, Physical Chemistry, effusion): rate ratio = sqrt(28.014 / 4.003) = 2.645 (node).

claims.text: At one temperature all gases share the same average kinetic energy, so lighter molecules move faster.
claims.source: Kinetic theory of gases: mean kinetic energy = (3/2) kT, independent of mass (Atkins, Physical Chemistry).

claims.text: In the stage's simulation (20,000 non-colliding particles in a 2-D box, a fixed time window) 1,166 helium particles reach the pinhole against 441 nitrogen, a ratio of about 2.6.
claims.source: Demo.tsx run(), seeds 100 (He) and 102 (N2); speeds drawn from a normal distribution with spread proportional to 1/sqrt(mass). The seeds were taken as the first tried (100 + gas index), not selected; other seeds gave helium:nitrogen ratios between about 2.6 and 2.9 (node). Neon and argon counts are also from the simulation and are not quoted in the lesson.

claims.text: The stage is a simplified model: two dimensions, no collisions between particles, a fixed number of particles, the same temperature for every gas. Real gases escape through small holes in three dimensions.
claims.source: Stage chip 'Simulated 2-D box, same temperature, no collisions'.

recall.question: At the same temperature, which gas leaks through a pinhole faster: hydrogen (2.0 g/mol) or oxygen (32.0 g/mol)?
options: Both leak at the same rate
recall.why: Rate scales as 1/sqrt(mass): sqrt(32.0 / 2.0) = sqrt(16) = 4, so lighter hydrogen leaks about 4 times as fast.
